verdict.rationale: Logseq documents a local HTTP API server with bearer-token auth and worked curl examples. Its single POST /api endpoint dispatches any plugin-API method, which gives an agent a route to read and write the graph. However, the server must first be enabled in the desktop app's Features settings and lives inside that app, so it is not truly GUI-free or headless. The method reference is community-driven, with no OpenAPI spec (probes 404) and no MCP server. A user also reports that the new DB version stops Claude/Codex from writing or updating pages, which undercuts the file-based agent route rather than the API itself. Missing for 10: truly headless operation without the desktop app, an official MCP server or vendor cloud API, first-party versioned method docs/OpenAPI, and hands-on corroboration of agent writes via the HTTP API.
